extras.limits_verbatim: per-object-cap: none. 200 IOPS on the 1 TB plan (from the billing cart). Port speed 100 Mbps.
extras.egress_verbatim: Metered: 2 TB / 4 TB / 8 TB per month on the 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 TB plans. No overage price published on the plan page. The 1 TB plan at 8 TB of transfer is a 8:1 ratio.
extras.chaining_verbatim: Single datacenter, 100 Mbps port on the storage line — the slowest port in this dossier and a hard limit on the serving workload.
extras.price_verbatim: $4.68/TB/mo on the promo (€4.17), **$9.38/TB/mo at renewal (€8.35)**. At 5 TB: five 1 TB plans at renewal = €41.75 = $46.90/mo = $9.38/TB. At 20 TB: €167 = $187.58/mo = $9.38/TB. This is the cleanest example of the trial-vs-steady-state trap in the lane: the advertised €4.17 is a first-term rate against a published 11.99 € list, and the renewal is exactly 2.0x.
extras.agent_focus: cheap-PAID lane — cheapest $/TB/month storage outside Europe for a self-funded buyer. Every candidate priced at the 5 TB and 20 TB tier as $ per TB per month, egress policy quoted verbatim, and payment friction for a non-US/non-EU buyer recorded. Deliberately excludes AWS/Azure/GCP/Alibaba/R2/B2/iDrive e2 (rejected). FX rates used throughout, taken 2026-10-21 from api.frankfurter.dev: EUR 0.89015, CAD 1.4046, INR 94.47, JPY 157.88, KRW 1325.57 per USD.
